changes.summary: The Privacy Policy now explains that the AI can read public web pages for you, and that those sites see your IP address.
The Privacy Policy now covers the RAM optimizer and skin lookups from Mojang, and the Acceptable Use Policy names Streamer mode instead of the removed Stream-proof HUD.
The privacy policy now covers Minecraft replay clips: they stay on your computer, and saving them as MP4 downloads the free ffmpeg converter from GitHub once.
The Minecraft client can show what you're playing on your Discord profile (rich presence), and the privacy policy now explains what it shares and how to switch it off.
Removed the part about Auoris staff sending actions to your Minecraft client, and the list of Minecraft accounts in use: that feature is gone.
Moderators, not only administrators, can now see which Minecraft accounts are running on an Auoris account.
Terms: Auoris staff can send actions to the Minecraft client; your own AI plans follow their providers' terms. Privacy: Minecraft ownership is proven without sending your token; link previews.
Privacy: the PC health scan also reads security settings (UAC, Secure Boot, Remote Desktop, SMB1)
Privacy: Gaming boost & PC health deep scan, and the optional Ask AI to look deeper
Usage now shows your Claude Code and Codex plan limits, read from what those apps report on your computer.
Pets: chatting with a pet sends the chat to the pet's AI model. Voice input and calls use speech recognition on your device or the web engine's online speech service.
Optional natural reading voice: the program and voice are downloaded once from GitHub and Hugging Face, then speech is made on your computer.
Pets: Auto-pick chooses which pet reads a prompt on your computer, and an optional second opinion sends the prompt to a second pet's model too.
Pets: the per-message 'No learning' switch is gone; instead you can switch each pet off completely.
Pets: we now say that each pet's last 60 analyses (with your prompt) are kept on your computer, that deleting all memories deletes them too, and that nothing is kept from incognito chats.
We added Auoris Pets (optional companions that read your prompt with the AI model you choose and keep memories only on your computer)
We added linked accounts (an optional public GitHub, Discord or Twitch name on your profile, and Discord and Twitch sign-in) and described connectors (MCP servers) you can add to the AI
Privacy policy: ban enforcement keeps a keyed hash of a banned account's email; covers /divide, sub-agents and auoris.md
Privacy policy: covers sub-agents the AI starts in Code mode
Privacy policy: covers /divide and auoris.md project notes
Auto mode and agent memory
Multi-model modes (/team, /split, /debate, @agents, private mode) and local usage/cost tracking
Security log also covers in-game moderation actions and announcements
Phone relay, Minecraft account ownership proof, owner security alerts
We now keep a private security log of changes to an account's standing (bans, staff roles and Plus status) for 12 months, used only to investigate misuse.
Added Auoris Extra (/extra), which sends a request to several AI models at once, and chat import (/import), which copies chats already on your computer into Auoris without uploading anything.
The Privacy Policy now says that the Minecraft accounts you run through Auoris (names and IDs only) are stored for up to 60 days and visible to you and to administrators for moderation.

Privacy Policy: added calls, defaults for presence and Minecraft sharing, GIF loading, the in-game /ai command and shared AI Project keys. Acceptable Use: Stream-proof HUD and other features must not be used to hide cheating from server staff or anticheat.
Removed the local Minecraft server host and public server addresses; the related Privacy and Acceptable Use clauses were deleted.
Privacy policy: emote you are playing is shared with other Auoris players; added how AI project messages are handled when someone asks the AI.

Local-network server addresses (name.local.auoris.org) are a new option that publishes your computer's private home-network address in public DNS, and servers can optionally be reached through a third-party tunnel service you set up yourself.

New optional feature: you can claim a public address like yourname.servers.auoris.org for a Minecraft server on your own computer. If you do, a public DNS record points that name at your computer's current IP address, so anyone can look it up. Address names must follow the Acceptable Use Policy.
Clarified that a ban on a network stays in place even if the banned account is deleted (so deleting an account can't undo a ban), alongside the earlier note about the hashes we keep to enforce bans.

We now remember a one-way hash of the last few networks you sign in from, only to enforce bans (administrators can block a banned account's networks from creating new accounts, and server owners can block a banned member's networks from rejoining that server; nobody can see any address). A suspension also stops a Plus subscription from renewing, with no refund for the period already paid.
Added our support contact address (auoris-support@googlegroups.com) to the legal documents.
Deleting your account now cancels an active Plus subscription for you instead of blocking deletion; sign-up now checks your age (the date of birth is not stored).

Added server Sparks to the Subscription Terms; stated the age requirement more clearly (13, or 16 where the law says so); clarified what malware scanning does, what game presence reads, how long reports are kept, and added trademark notices.
First version of the Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, Acceptable Use Policy, Subscription and Gift Terms, and Copyright policy.
